title: The coin toss and the wind: defer, receive or pick an end (and why it matters in College Park today)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. It was last updated Oct 12. The original football-film-room repo can't be read from this scheduled run (GitHub said access to it "is not enabled for this session"). So there are no new misses of yours to target. This lesson is a new concept for today's windiest game, Penn State at Maryland (gusts of 28–33 mph at kickoff), the board's Under.

The big idea: the wind blows the same way all game. The teams don't stay put.They switch ends after every quarter. So each team gets the wind at its back for two quarters.The coin toss, and the choice at halftime, decide which two.

Letters match the list below. Yellow = the wind. The chart shows one team's four quarters.

  1. A · The wind. Here it blows left to right. A strong wind is about 15 mph or more; gusts near 30 change kicks a lot.
  2. B · The goal you defend. Choosing "the wind" really means choosing which goal to defend, with the wind at your back.
  3. C · The goal you attack. Kicking toward it, field goals and punts carry farther. Kicking the other way, a 45-yarder can fall short.
  4. D · The switch. Teams change ends after the 1st and 3rd quarters, and the second half starts with a new choice.So if you have the wind in Q1, you're into it in Q2.
  5. E · The 4th quarter. That's when the wind matters most: last drives, long kicks to win.To have the wind in Q4, a team takes the end that puts it into the wind in Q3.

The toss: the winner picks one thing. Receive, kick, or the goal to defend. Or "defer": let the other team pick now and pick first in the second half.The loser picks from what's left. If one team takes the ball, the other takes the wind.Most teams defer, so they get the ball to start the second half. In a strong wind, some coaches take the wind instead.

Real example, NFL: Dec 27, 2015, Patriots at Jets, overtime. The Patriots won the toss and chose to kick off so they would have the wind.The Jets took the ball, drove for a TD (Eric Decker's catch) and won 26-20. Under the overtime rules then, a TD on the first drive ended the game.Taking the wind gave away the ball, and they never got it back.

Today, College Park: AccuWeather has gusts of 28–33 mph at kickoff, easing to about 12 mph after halftime.So the 1st quarter is the windiest. The team into the wind in Q1 will likely run more and punt sooner.That's part of the Penn State-Maryland Under: fewer deep balls, shorter field goals, more clock running.Friday, Pittsburgh: in rain, Denver's Wil Lutz missed from 53. Bad weather shrinks the range a coach trusts.

In the drill: before the first snap of each quarter, check the flags on the goalposts. Write which way they blow.The offense into a strong wind: call run more often, and expect short passes and an early punt on 4th-and-medium.

Check yourself: a team has the wind in the 3rd quarter. Does it have the wind in the 4th? (No. Teams switch ends after the 3rd, so it's into the wind.)

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 6: Situations)

quiz.q: Teams switch ends after which quarters?
o: After the 1st and 3rd quarters (and the second half starts fresh)
quiz.w: They switch after the 1st and 3rd, and the second half begins with a new choice. So each team gets the wind for two quarters.

quiz.q: A team wants the wind at its back in the 4th quarter. In the 3rd quarter it should be…
quiz.w: Teams switch ends after the 3rd. Into the wind in Q3 means with the wind in Q4.

quiz.q: What does "defer" mean at the coin toss?
o: Let the other team choose now, and choose first in the second half
quiz.w: Deferring gives your choice to the second half. Most teams defer so they get the ball to start the 3rd quarter.

quiz.q: Dec 2015, overtime: the Patriots chose to kick off to have the wind. What happened?
o: They won on a long FG
The Jets drove for a TD and won 26-20
quiz.w: The Jets took the ball and scored a TD on the first drive, which ended the game under those rules.
